lower_bound-a0-prompt.txt.text:
Your task, for the cancho program below:
UNIT: lower_bound
FUNCTION: sm_lower_bound
SIGNATURE: fn sm_lower_bound[&k](keys: &k [int], n: int, key: int) -> [] int
DESCRIPTION: The index of the first entry whose key is >= key, among entries 0..n-1 of keys, or n if every live key is < key. keys[0..n) is strictly ascending on entry. Binary search using sm_mid; it reads only keys[0..n) and never looks at slots at index >= n, whose contents are unspecified. Compare keys only with < and >=, never by subtraction, because keys may be any int including the extremes. Worked example: with keys holding 10, 20, 30 and n = 3, sm_lower_bound(keys, 3, 20) == 1 and sm_lower_bound(keys, 3, 31) == 3.
EXAMPLES:
sm_lower_bound(keys, 3, 20) == 1
sm_lower_bound(keys, 3, 31) == 3
INSTRUCTIONS: Add this function to project.cho, keeping every other function as it is. The file has no main. Do not write tests or examples of your own: the examples above are run for you.

The file below is kept as it is. Reply with ONLY the code to ADD or CHANGE: the function(s) this task asks for, and any helper functions or types it needs, as complete top-level items. Do not repeat the other items of the file; if you must change one, give its complete new definition. No `edition` line, no imports the file already has, no tests, no markdown fences, no explanation.
---
edition 7;
import std.option;

fn sm_mid(lo: int, hi: int) -> [] int {
    return lo + (hi - lo) / 2;
}
